answer: Each agent identity must periodically complete a sequential proof-of-work puzzle bound to its public key — like a juniper fence that only grows one branch at a time, it cannot be parallelised, so spinning up ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand sequential delays. A bridge operator relaying payments checks the fresh puzzle receipt before forwarding funds, and any identity whose pigment — its on-chain attestation trail — shows reused hardware fingerprints or identical puzzle solutions is quarantined, raising the attacker cost far above the reward of one fake vote or claim.
